target.title: fix(vault): cancel unread response body on non-ok HTTP responses
target.body:
## Summary

**What**: Cancel unread HTTP response body before throwing on non-ok status in Vault secret resolver.

**Why**: Two problems: (1) Vault error responses (403, 404, etc.) leave a dangling stream that wastes memory and can cause connection stalls (CVE-2024-24750). (2) Failing to cancel the body triggers Node.js "unread response body" warnings.

**What changed**: Added `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` (fire-and-forget) before throwing on non-ok responses in both `resolveVaultTokenFromJwt` and `readVaultSecret`. NOT changed: any error handling logic, logging, or response processing for ok responses.

**merge-risk**: Low. Only 2 lines added — cancellation before throw on error paths. No impact on the happy path (ok responses are unchanged).

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**:
Node.js fetch (undici) requires explicit body consumption or cancellation on all code paths. Without consuming or cancelling the body when throwing on non-ok responses:
- Memory leak (CVE-2024-24750, undici <6.6.1)
- Connections not returned to HTTP/1.1 keep-alive pool
- Node.js emits "unread response body" warning (v18+)
- `body.cancel()` has a known race condition (undici#2009) where it can throw `ERR_INVALID_STATE` — the `.catch(() => undefined)` guards against this

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js v25.9.0 on Linux (x86_64), direct HTTP fetch to httpbin.org

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
script -q -c "node _scripts/evidence-vault-body-cancel.mjs" /dev/null
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
================================================================
  Evidence: response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)
  PR #109980 — Vault non-ok HTTP response handling
================================================================
  Node.js  v25.9.0
  HEAD     6ea0d815d9af4bedb2b9168d4ebc53a159be1d44
================================================================

--- Part 1: body.cancel() API exists and is callable ---
  typeof resp.body?.cancel: function
  resp.body.locked before: false
  resp.body.locked after:  false
  -> body.cancel() works without throwing

--- Part 2: .catch(() => undefined) guards against cancel() throwing ---
  Known issue: body.cancel() can throw ERR_INVALID_STATE
  (github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/2009)

  Without .catch():
    Error caught: TypeError: Invalid state: ReadableStream is locked

  With .catch(() => undefined):
    No error — caught by .catch()

--- Part 3: Security & resource impact ---
  CVE-2024-24750: Memory leak in Node.js fetch when body
  is not consumed or cancelled (undici <6.6.1).
  Fixed by always cancelling or consuming response bodies.

--- Part 4: Verification for PR #109980 changes ---
  [...]
  Code pattern in both:
    if (!response.ok) {
      response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);
      throw new Error(...);
    }
  [...]
  5. .catch(() => undefined) guards undici#2009 race condition
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
- `body.cancel()` is a valid, callable API
- The `.catch(() => undefined)` is necessary to guard against the known race condition where `cancel()` can throw `TypeError: Invalid state: ReadableStream is locked` (undici#2009)
- Without `.catch()`, a cancel() failure would propagate and mask the actual error being thrown
- The fire-and-forget pattern ensures the error is thrown immediately without awaiting stream cleanup

**What was not tested**:
- Real Vault server with non-ok responses (integration test). The existing vault extension tests cover the happy path and use mocked HTTP; testing against a real Vault server returning 403 would require a live Vault instance and is not needed for this fix.

## Tests and validation

**Unit tests**: All 29 vault extension tests pass with the change.

```bash
npx vitest run extensions/vault/
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
```

**Evidence script**: Reproducible in CI or local with:
```bash
HEAD_HASH=$(git rev-parse HEAD) script -q -c "node _scripts/evidence-vault-body-cancel.mjs" /dev/null
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] This change has been verified with unit tests (29/29 pass)
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary
